title: Item 1
statement: Less than 100% belief (full certainty) in the Gospel will not secure redemption.
suggested_questions: Do believers have a mechanism that can legitimately provide them full certainty on propositions outside their immediate sensations? What is that mechanism, and how was the reliability of that mechanism assessed?
Does salvific belief require going beyond the available evidence for the Gospel in some cases, and is this epistemic "leaping" beyond the evidence outside the bounds of rationality?
If salvific belief in the Gospel can be accomplished at less than full certainty, what is the epistemic threshold at which redemption is rewarded?
If someone honestly admits a sliver of doubt in the Gospel, is this person unredeemed?

title: Item 2
statement: The explosion in the availability of porn is the greatest single spiritual threat facing young Christians today.
suggested_questions: What damage does porn do to young believers?
Do Christians struggle less with pornography than non-believers?
What can Christians do to effectively combat the temptation of porn?
Does habitual porn consumption warrant the spouse's serious contemplation of divorce? [See item #152 ]

title: Item 3
statement: Christians who are doubting their faith should avoid examining arguments and evidence against Christianity.
suggested_questions: Can doubt on any issue be a legitimate and rational permanent position, or does doubt always need to be resolved?

Is there any tension in the position of a Christian who maintains Muslims should read more about the Christian Gospel while encouraging their Christian friends to avoid Muslim books and proselytizers?
What kind of diet of books, publications, and media contrary to Christianity should Christians maintain if they wish to be both honest seekers and strong Christians?
Is it unhealthy to regularly (provisionally) discard the foundations of Christianity to see whether it can be successfully reconstructed?

title: Item 4
statement: Differences in moral opinions among Christians are due to our sinful natures and would not exist were everyone right with God.
suggested_questions: What is the composition or balance of the various sources of moral knowledge available to us? (These sources might include the Holy Spirit, the Bible, or an innate moral sense.)
Can a Christian be truly blind to sin that may be producing their incorrect moral conclusions?
Are improper moral conclusions a reliable indicator of sin in the individual holding the improper conclusion, or are they more an indicator of poor shepherding or disciplining?

title: Item 5
statement: For Christians right with God, the guidance of the Holy Spirit cannot be confused with the deceptions of Satan.
suggested_questions: What is the process required to distinguish between the Holy Spirit and Satan? Is this process fool-proof?
What is the best biblical source for the proper procedure to rigorously "try the spirits"?

title: Item 6
statement: Humans can secure, but then later lose their salvation.
suggested_questions: For those who lean affirmative on this item, do these humans clearly know both when they secure their salvation and lose their salvation?
What is the particular threshold at which a true believer will lose their salvation?
Is the threshold at which one will lose their salvation based on behaviors or based on the degree of belief?

title: Item 7
statement: It is rational to first explore whether a particular God and his alleged actions are moral before believing in and worshiping that God.
suggested_questions: Are honest seekers bound by their commitment to rationality to first morally assess candidate Gods before believing in any of them?
Is there a legitimate standard of morality that we can use to assess candidate Gods for their moral character prior to believing in any of the candidate Gods? What is the source of that standard?
If a candidate God is known to have His followers throw living infants off the tops of mountains, can this candidate God be rationally rejected on some kind of clear and rigorous moral basis?

title: Item 8
statement: Unborn humans and born humans have equal value and deserve equal rights.
suggested_questions: Are the rights given to unborn humans derived from the Christian God, or are there secular arguments granting unborn humans their rights?
Is there any instance in which an unborn human can be killed, such as if/when other moral considerations take precedence?

title: Item 9
statement: An immersion-in-water baptism is essential for redemption.
suggested_questions: For those who lean affirmative on this item, does God make exceptions for believers who have little access to water?
If immersion-in-water baptism is merely a post-redemption command by God, what method and timeliness would constitute obedience to this command?

title: Item 10
statement: My understanding and practice of Christianity have become less conservative over the past five years.
suggested_questions: Has your move to a less/more conservative understanding and practice of Christianity been caused by or resulted in a move to a less/more conservative congregation of believers?
Which of the following domains of belief have been trending more/less conservative? Inerrancy of Scriptures
Sexuality
Lifestyles (E.g., Alcohol, modesty, language)
Doctrinal orthodoxy/traditions
Sacraments/Ecclesiastical practices (E.g., Women in church leadership)
Notions of divine punishment (E.g., A literal burning Hell)
Requirements of redemption

title: Item 11
statement: We must sometimes ignore our moral intuitions to act truly morally.
suggested_questions: Can moral intuitions be wrong?
In spite of being occasionally wrong, are our moral intuitions useful?
How do moral intuitions fit into the constellation of moral tools that allow us to uncover moral facts?
What is the best way to distinguish moral intuition form mere emotions?

title: Item 12
statement: Most young people who abandon Christianity do so because they want to sin.
suggested_questions: Is there statistical data to demonstrate young people abandoning Christianity do so to satisfy their sinful desires?
If there is currently no available statistical data to uncover the reasons for apostasy among young people, how might we design a legitimate survey to reveal actual reasons for apostasy?
How might we respond to Muslims who claim Christians choose Christianity because they want to sin instead of following the high moral standards of Allah?

title: Item 13
statement: A high though not absolute (100%) degree of belief in the Gospel is sufficient for redemption.
suggested_questions: We may want to keep comments for this item and the three related items in the comments section for item #1.

title: Item 14
statement: The pursuit of pleasure in this life while aware that millions within reach remain unGospelled is sinful.
suggested_questions: Is the recent apparent decreasing passion for souls due to the recent move away from the notion of a literal burning Hell?
Should the lifestyles of the Apostles serve as an example to those who have a passion for souls today?
What degree of pursuit for earthly comforts and pleasures while millions are perishing clearly constitutes sin?

title: Item 15
statement: An eternally painful punishment for even one sin is justified due to God's perfect righteousness.
suggested_questions: Does perfect righteousness logically require eternal painful punishment for sinners?
How do we answer the common refrain that infinite punishment for finite sins is intrinsically unjust?

title: Item 16
statement: Being made in the "image of God" refers to humans' moral perception reflecting God's moral standard.
suggested_questions: Can our moral perception, given the degree of its inaccuracy, be considered a reflection of God's moral perception?

title: Item 17
statement: Learning the original biblical languages, such as Hebrew and Greek, is necessary for a proper interpretation of the Scriptures.
suggested_questions: Is it reasonable to expect every pastor to have a grasp of the original languages?
Do those well-versed in the original languages more commonly converge on single doctrinal positions?

title: Item 18
statement: Setting up a theocracy in a country would be contrary to God's plan today.
suggested_questions: What degree of political involvement is proper for Christians today?
How should Christians respond to governments that attempt to set up a Christian theocracy?
Should Christians or Muslims attempt to establish as law their standards of modesty or decency?

title: Item 19
statement: Over 50% of genuine Christians today attend religious services primarily to be entertained.
suggested_questions: Should aesthetics be considered when a congregation is 1) planning the construction of a building in which to meet, 2) hiring a pastor, or when buying musical instruments?
All things being equal, is it better to have a good-looking and humorous pastor who will attract more people to the services?

title: Item 20
statement: Intentionally consuming alcohol is sinful.
suggested_questions: Not that many decades ago, many Christians condemned the consumption of alcohol. What changed?
Is intoxication the proper threshold at which drinking becomes sinful?

title: Item 21
statement: Homosexual acts are always sinful.
suggested_questions: In the Bible, homosexuality was causally tied to the destruction of the offending society. Can we make testable predictions today based on the increase in homosexuality?
Are modern Christian correct in their acceptance of those with homosexual desires who do not act on their desires?

title: Item 22
statement: A sudden rapture of Christians into Heaven will occur within 20 years.
suggested_questions: Will the bodies of those raptured be transformed into something different from their earthly bodies prior to their ascension?
What signs are most indicative of the return of Jesus?
What has led to the apparent recent drop in the number of prophecies of an end-times date?
Are the perennial expectations of the return of Jesus across generations a reason to doubt the promise or the interpretation of the promise?

title: Item 23
statement: Musical performances are overused in Christian churches today.
suggested_questions: Is the evoking of emotions with music and other aesthetics to complement the moving of the Holy Spirit proper?
Are there musical genres that are intrinsically satanic or ungodly?
Is it proper to introduce music to the congregation that was produced by someone who was during the creation of the music or who is now an apostate?

title: Item 24
statement: It is possible that what I feel are moral intuitions are merely my emotions.
suggested_questions: Are there passages in Scripture that instruct us how to distinguish between our emotions and the moving of the Holy Spirit?

Many of the Israelite soldiers likely had to ignore or block out their moral intuitions when asked to kill Canaanite kids. What might be an effective technique or approach to use when we also have to violate our moral intuitions?
Is there a process through which one can exercise their moral faculties to eliminate emotional bias to arrive at clear moral knowledge?

title: Item 25
statement: There are fewer incidences of illnesses and early deaths among true Christians than among non-Christians.
suggested_questions: Will the recent COVID crisis eventually reveal that fewer Christians or more devoted Christians died at much lower rates than did the general population?
To what degree and in what way is the promise that God's eye is on both the sparrow and those he loves detectable?

title: Item 26
statement: I have found no argument against the God of the Bible worth taking seriously.
suggested_questions: What is the significance of those with more years in ministry being more likely to encounter arguments against the Bible worth taking seriously?
Should the average Christian be more exposed or less exposed to arguments against the God of the Bible?

title: Item 27
statement: God does not publicly heal amputees in order to avoid the elimination of our free will to choose or reject Him.
suggested_questions: Does undeniable evidence of God take away our free will to refuse to follow God? Or can someone convinced that God exists still reject God?

Why do miracles seem to be confined to the boundary of what is physically possible such as a remission or elimination of cancer, instead of the healing of amputees or the resurrection of someone dead for several weeks?
Are healings tightly tied to the degree of faith in the one praying for healing? If so, can this correlation be made rigorous in a study?

title: Item 28
statement: Introducing sex toys and costumes into a Christian marriage is sinful.
suggested_questions: For those leaning towards the affirmative on this item, what is the source of your moral code on this?
Is dressing your spouse up to appear very distant from who they actually are to make them more sexually appealing sinful?

title: Item 29
statement: Unbelievers without the cosmic meaning the Christian God provides feel hopeless and emotionally unsatisfied.
suggested_questions: How can we rigorously test this notion? Or is such a test impossible since it cannot be known when unbelievers are lying?
Is it possible that personal meaning derived from children or the compassionate assistance of others can eliminate the longing for cosmic meaning?

title: Item 30
statement: Had God the Father not resurrected Jesus until 100 days after his death, He would have been unjust.
suggested_questions: How long could God have kept Jesus dead before He would have been unjust?
Had God kept Jesus eternally dead, would He have been unjust?
Is the critical notion here the need for Jesus to die? Could he have been resurrected minutes after his death and still have accomplished redemption for sinners?
What is the actual calculus for redemption? What was the debt, and what was the payment?

title: Item 31
statement: The Earth is flat, not spherical.
suggested_questions: It might be interesting to imagine responses to this item 1,500 years ago. What might have been the reasoning offered by those believing in a flat Earth?

title: Item 32
statement: The ethnic distribution in my local congregation largely reflects the ethnic balance found in my community.
suggested_questions: Is it proper and expected that ethnic groups would form their own environments of worship, even though they are worshiping the same God?
What advantages does a more integrated church have?

title: Item 33
statement: Christians in Heaven will not shed tears for the damned because they will have the perfectly just mind of God.
suggested_questions: Some skeptics of an excruciatingly painful Hell might claim the longer that your loved one is tormented in Hell, the more difficult it will be to hold back tears and the notion that there is something unjust about the punishment. Will God transform our minds to experience the same wrath towards sinners that He experiences? If not, how might Heaven remain enjoyable?

title: Item 34
statement: The large number of professed Christians is a good argument for the truth of the Gospel.
suggested_questions: Is the popularity of Christianity ever a good argument for its veracity?
What implication does the notion that "narrow is the way" have on the claim that Christianity's popularity speaks to its truth?

title: Item 35
statement: Anal sex is sinful, even with a spouse.
suggested_questions: Why are Christian men and Christian women so split on this moral question?
Is there a clear and unequivocal moral standard that might quickly resolve this moral quandary?

title: Item 36
statement: Refusing to fight for one's country in a justified war is sinful.
suggested_questions: Are we morally obliged to fight for our country in a just war?
What is the moral calculus that would ground this moral obligation?

title: Item 37
statement: I adjust my degree of belief in God up and down to map to the degree of the confirming/disconfirming evidence for God I encounter.
suggested_questions: We adjust our degree of certainty up and down based on confirming and disconfirming evidence in other inquiries in life. What makes the inquiry into considerations of candidate Gods or of the Christian God different?
Is there any other domain of life in which a binary "I believe" or "I disbelieve" yields better results than the more nuanced mapping of our degree of belief to the degree of the evidence?
Would the author of rationality ask us to give up rational belief in which we adjust our degree of belief to map to the degree of the relevant evidence in respect to our belief in Him?

title: Item 38
statement: The satisfaction of human emotions, such as the hope for an afterlife and the desire for forgiveness, is evidence of the Gospel's truth.
suggested_questions: Some writers, such as CS Lewis, have suggested that the existence of our emotions implies the necessity of the fulfillment of our emotions. What is the rigorous argument behind this idea?

Other religions competing with Christianity have often been accused of promoting their religion by highlighting all the emotional needs their religion can allegedly fulfill. Could they also use a formulation of the argument that the existence of emotions implies a necessary fulfillment of those emotions?

title: Item 39
statement: I have doubts about the truth of Christianity about once a month.
suggested_questions: Is there something intrinsically sinful or irrational about doubting the existence of God?
Is it healthy to regularly review from the foundation of one's faith? Or is it something to be avoided?

title: Item 40
statement: Christianity becomes more likely true if a major competing ideology is demonstrated to be false.
suggested_questions: Does the possibly infinite number of ideologies in competition with Christianity make this notion logically/mathematically untrue?

Do you think Christian apologists too often lean on this notion (either explicitly or implicitly) when focusing on the flaws in major competing ideologies today? In other words, do they believe they have defended Christianity if they simply point out the transparent incoherencies in other ideologies?

title: Item 41
statement: It is sinful to attempt to statistically test the promises God gave Christians for this earthly life.
suggested_questions: Since the continued faithfulness of God (an inductive result) is often invoked as evidence for God, is there anything that would make a rigorous quantification of this continued faithfulness of God sinful?
Many characters in the Bible explicitly tested God in some way. Has such testing become anathema to God for post-Jesus believers?
Did Elijah violate any divine injunction not to test God when he set up the contest with the false prophets?

title: Item 42
statement: Acupuncture and homeopathy have real medicinal value.
suggested_questions: Do Christian need more education in proper standards of evidence?
Are Christians more inclined to follow alternative medicine? If so, why?

title: Item 43
statement: There will be a rapture of Christians to Heaven before serious tribulation is unleashed on the Earth.
suggested_questions: Will Jesus and the Saints travel through literal space to Heaven? If not, why would there need to be a meeting in the air?

Was there an improper translation of "quickly" in Revelations 22:12? Could not the word have instead been "slowly" if "a day is like a thousand years"? Would this not have provided more or equivalent exegetical content?
Under what conditions can a generation of Christians honestly believe Christ will return within their generation?

title: Item 44
statement: Christian parents should completely sever ties with their apostate children.
suggested_questions: Are the injunctions to refrain from eating and fellowshipping with apostate Christians also applicable to apostate children? Why or why not?

title: Item 45
statement: The absurdity of a universe with no moral standard makes the existence of a moral law-giver logically necessary.
suggested_questions: What logical argument makes a moral law-giver logically necessary? Could God have created a universe in which he found no need to impose morality on the creatures within that universe?
Is it just the existence of humans in our universe that makes morality necessary, or would a universe with only lesser animals require a moral law-giver? If so, what is the critical distinction?

title: Item 46
statement: Civil marriages performed without reference to God are legitimate marriages in the eyes of God.
suggested_questions: What elements comprise the full set of requisites that would legitimate a marriage?
If invoking God in the ceremony is not necessary, what authority or principle could be invoked that would legitimize the commitment?

title: Item 47
statement: Most teens in Christian families should be sent to a Christian high school or be home-schooled.
suggested_questions: What are the primary reasons for church schools or home-schooling today?
What negative consequences are there for children who are church schooled or home-schooled?

title: Item 48
statement: The main weekly service should primarily be a time for evangelism.
suggested_questions: When and where are legitimate times and places for evangelism?
Should congregation members invite unbelievers to worship with them?

title: Item 49
statement: All of the Gospels were written within twenty years of the crucifixion.
suggested_questions: Is understanding the history of the written Gospels at all important to the decision whether or not to believe in the Gospel?
Do ministers spend enough time teaching the history of the Gospels?

title: Item 50
statement: Humans can sincerely believe they have been redeemed when they have not been.
suggested_questions: How might it be possible for an sincere person to fail to realize they have not actually been redeemed?
Does an affirmative response to this item entail that someone can "know" in their heart they are redeemed, and yet be wrong?
How can we detect those who are certain they are redeemed, yet who are actually not?
How can we convince someone who is certain they are redeemed that they are actually not?

title: Item 51
statement: Church leaders should study philosophy in addition to the Bible.
suggested_questions: There has been a renaissance of philosophy within many branches of Christianity that once disparaged it. Is this trend generally positive?
When the Scriptures refer to "vain philosophies" in Colossians 2:8, what precisely is it referring to?

title: Item 52
statement: Christians can never be fully certain they have been redeemed.
suggested_questions: There appears to be some tension between the bulk of the credences on this item and item #50. How can we resolve this apparent tension?

title: Item 53
statement: There are cases in which one can know with full certainty that God will answer their prayer as requested.
suggested_questions: What are the conditions in these cases in which you can know your petitionary prayer will be answered?

James, in the context of petitionary prayer, claims doubt of any degree should not be present. How might this be reconciled with the notion we can never know with full certainty that our petitionary prayer will be answered as requested? (James 1:6) Is the "lack of doubt" and "full certainty" different in some way?
Based on James 1:6, shouldn't we have full certainty that our petitionary prayers will be answered?

title: Item 54
statement: Women should not teach men on spiritual topics in the local church.
suggested_questions: Is there a clear Scriptural delineation between contexts in which women can teach men and contexts in which they cannot teach men?
Is there a rational reason other than the fact Adam was created before Eve and that Eve was deceived to refuse to allow women to teach men?

title: Item 55
statement: A 50% degree of confidence in the Gospel is sufficient for redemption.
suggested_questions: Is this a wholly arbitrary threshold for the degree of sufficient belief, or is there something substantial about the 50% mark?
Can a child with an Islamic father and a Christian mother simply split their confidence between the two candidate faiths to hedge their bets? How about a 1%/99% split in favor of the Christian God?

title: Item 56
statement: A "mustard seed" degree of belief in the Gospel is sufficient for redemption.
suggested_questions: In the attached graphic, survey participants provided credences that positioned the faith of a mustard seed above even a "high" degree of belief. Was not the use of "mustard seed" employed by Jesus to make it very clear that the degree of faith was not high?

title: Item 57
statement: Christians who are doubting their faith should surround themselves with strong Christians to reduce their doubt.
suggested_questions: Can we also recommend that Muslims doubting their faith surround themselves with strong Muslims to reduce their doubt? What is an impartial, relevant principle we can provide all honest seekers? Is there one? Need there be one? Why or why not?
Should we also recommend that doubters read books written in support of other faiths or non-belief?

title: Item 58
statement: Praying earnestly to a proposed God in the hope that he will reveal himself is an irrational way to assess his existence.
suggested_questions: Should this principle/practice be applied to all candidate Gods, such as Allah and the Hindu gods?
How can we coherently answer Muslims who claim to have come to Allah in this way?

Is there any danger that 1) yearning for a God you don't currently believe in and 2) praying to that God in the hope he will give you recognition of this existence will lead to a false conclusion that He is real?

title: Item 59
statement: Unredeemed sinners deserve eternal torment.
suggested_questions: Is there any type of coherent calculus we can invoke when determining what offense deserves what punishment?
Is this punishment of eternal torment based on justice, or is it based on God's wrathful nature?
What is the argument against the simple divine forgiveness of offenses that humans find possible?

Should not parents, instead of snickering at their children's chocolate-faced lies about the missing cookies, severely punish such children as consistently as possible with the punishment God deems appropriate for the offense?

title: Item 60
statement: Christians who are doubting Christianity should not seek out or re-examine arguments and evidence against Christianity.
suggested_questions: Is there any duty for Christians to hide the existence of materials that might lead weaker Christians away from God?
Is there a relevant, universal principle consistent across both Christianity and Islam that could be applied to weak Christians and weak Muslims alike?

title: Item 61
statement: Christians can know with high certainty whether any suffering they experience is due to sin, chance, or divine testing.
suggested_questions: Will God ever send suffering as punishment without making it very clear the suffering is punishment for sin?
Can Christians ever know with certainty the reason for their suffering?

title: Item 62
statement: In ten years, fewer true Christians will be regularly attending a physical church.
suggested_questions: What are the emerging alternatives to physical churches?
Is the physical meeting of believers a biblical mandate in this age of digital interactions?
Would returning to fellowship in homes be an acceptable option to meeting in buildings collectively purchased by attendees?
Are there any natural limits to the size of a congregation?

title: Item 63
statement: Humans have no epistemic obligation to apply rigorous standards of evidence in their assessments of candidate Gods.
suggested_questions: What is the best passage of Scripture that establishes standards of evidence when choosing between candidate Gods?

Would it be appropriate to take a leap of faith toward a particular candidate God when the standards of evidence yield no strong conclusion? And how might we determine to which candidate God we should apply this leap of faith?

title: Item 64
statement: As can be shown statistically, believers live healthier lives due to the help of the Holy Spirit to live righteously.
suggested_questions: If you were to design a study that might demonstrate the power of the Holy Spirit results in healthier lives for believers, what would be the essential components of that study?

Will the assistance to the human will of the Holy Spirit be consistent across cultures? Or do some cultures have social expectations that could outperform the strength of will provided by the Holy Spirit?

title: Item 65
statement: Everyone holds a degree of confidence above the degree of the relevant evidence for at least some propositions.
suggested_questions: Based on the responses, humans cannot limit their degrees of confidence to the degree of the relevant evidence. What is the reason behind this inability to restrain belief to the degree of the evidence?
If someone told you they honestly limited their degree of confidence to the degree of the relevant evidence, how would you verbally respond or show them they were wrong?

title: Item 66
statement: If God were to indisputably reveal his existence to someone, this would eliminate their free will.
suggested_questions: Based on the responses, God is not hidden or silent because he does not want to violate our free will. What are other possible reasons God might not clearly reveal himself?

title: Item 67
statement: Presuppositional apologetics is an effective way to evangelize.
suggested_questions: If you hold to Christian presuppositionalism, how do you typically respond to Muslim presuppositionalistic arguments?
Are presuppositionalists abandoning logic and reason when they choose the Bible as a starting point without feeling the need to supply evidence to establish this?

title: Item 68
statement: Redemption required that Jesus experience physical suffering.
suggested_questions: What are the precise elements that had to be present for redemption to take place? Death? What length?
Blood? How much?
Suffering? How much?
How do these elements combine to accomplish redemption?

title: Item 69
statement: God is pleased when someone takes a "leap of faith" beyond the available evidence to fully believe in Him.
suggested_questions: Some claim that mustering up faith beyond the less-than-certain evidence to reach full certainty is intrinsically irrational, as it is in other domains of life. How might we respond?

If we add stipulations to prevent us from taking leaps of faith toward just any proposition, will our stipulations necessarily include non-arbitrary factors that must themselves be established with evidence?

title: Item 70
statement: I could be wrong in my belief that Christianity is true.
suggested_questions: On what propositions can we simply end our inquiry at some point and be certain we could not be wrong?

Some Christians regularly review their faith, provisionally suspending their belief, and reevaluating the arguments for and against Christianity to ensure they have not overlooked anything. Is this a noble or dangerous process?

title: Item 71
statement: Humans did not evolve from lower forms of life.
suggested_questions: Does the trend seem to be a movement toward or away from young-earth creationism?

title: Item 72
statement: The Christian God will definitely reveal himself to all who honestly seek Him.
suggested_questions: Nearly all respondents strongly believe God will reveal himself to those who honestly seek Him. In what form are the revelations? Transcendent states of consciousness?
Material evidence?
Arguments from Christian philosophy?
Inexplicable emotions?
A dream?
A vision?
A "Road to Damascus" experience?
Improbable events?
Are there any items in the list above that would not be a component of revelation God would not use?

title: Item 73
statement: Prayer works, and this is statistically demonstrable.
suggested_questions: Given the number of Christians praying, should answered prayers be statistically evidenced?
How might we design a study of the efficacy of the prayers for safety during COVID?
Are there any legitimate "outs" that Christians could invoke if the statistics show zero or negative effects of prayer?

title: Item 74
statement: A devout Muslim who has consciously rejected the Christian God is knowingly worshiping a false God.
suggested_questions: This item had a fairly well-defined split in the responses. What are the relevant verses?
How might we design a study to tease out the truth on this issue?

title: Item 75
statement: Prayer studies conducted by Christian researchers can demonstrate whether or not prayer works.
suggested_questions: Can prayer studies by anyone demonstrate the efficacy of prayer?
Are answered prayers common enough to show up in general statistics?
Which of the following types of prayers are most likely to be statistically evidenced? Prayers for safety
Prayers for healing
Prayers for financial protection
Prayers for material desires
Prayers for souls

title: Item 76
statement: Jesus had the same capacity to sin as have all other humans.
suggested_questions: If Jesus was fully divine, and if God cannot sin, how then could Jesus have the capacity to sin?
If Jesus could have actually sinned, what would have been the consequences if He had?

title: Item 77
statement: Christians are still regularly gifted with the ability to speak in tongues today.
suggested_questions: Must an interpreter accompany the one speaking in tongues?
Can glossolalia be tested as authentic in any way?

title: Item 78
statement: Christians cannot be mistaken when they feel what seems to be God-given joy and peace.
suggested_questions: If Christians can be mistaken, what is the precise process or mechanism to prevent mistakes?
If Christians cannot be mistaken, what is the mechanism that provides this certainty, and was that mechanism itself tested for reliability?

title: Item 79
statement: In my local church over the past 5 years, there has been at least a 30% decline in regular church attendees in their 20s.
suggested_questions: What are the trends? Will the downward trend reverse post-COVID?
What might churches do to trigger a return to the pews?

title: Item 80
statement: Global warming is not actually happening.
suggested_questions: Might church-sponsored courses on science and scientific thinking be helpful to Christians?
Are there any dangers in teaching rigorous scientific thinking, such as an eagerness to test every claim before assigning degrees of confidence in each claim tested?

title: Item 81
statement: Doctrinal differences among real Christians are primarily due to honest misunderstandings of the Scriptures.
suggested_questions: Assuming that God made doctrinal knowledge easily accessible, what is the correct hermeneutical process, and what components are essential to that process?
What are other causes behind incorrect doctrinal beliefs?
Is an understanding of the original biblical languages an essential component of proper hermeneutics? ( See Item #17 )

title: Item 82
statement: A much greater percentage of humans will die in wars over the next 100 years than in the past 100 years.
suggested_questions: Are we in the period of the "end times"?
Are sources such as Steven Pinker's "The Better Angels of our Nature" that present an optimistic view of the future of humanity overtly biased or somehow misguided?

title: Item 83
statement: Divorce is justified in a case in which a spouse is not sexually unfaithful, but is romantically unfaithful.
suggested_questions: What are the rigorously delineated conditions under which divorce is warranted?
Can the person who has divorced the other remarry in these cases?

title: Item 84
statement: At least 20% of the young people who leave Christianity do so because they were exposed to secular arguments against God.
suggested_questions: What is the best source to substantiate the actual percentage of young people who have left do to secular arguments against God?
How can Christian parents best innoculate their children from secular arguments?
What is the proper understanding of what seems to be a promise in Proverbs 22:6: " Train up a child in the way he should go ; even when he is old he will not depart from it."

title: Item 85
statement: The probability of Jesus' resurrection will be close to 100% in the minds of everyone who honestly looks at the evidence.
suggested_questions: Should the inductive improbability of an actual resurrection factor into the assessment of the probability of Jesus' resurrection?
Does the long period between the alleged date of the resurrection and its written documentation warrant any doubt about whether the event was fabricated to some degree?
Can someone slightly doubt the resurrection and still become a Christian?

title: Item 86
statement: The suffering of animals in the world today is a direct result of the sins of Adam and Eve.
suggested_questions: Is having animals suffer for the sins of humans consistent with justice?
Is divine justice so distant from the understanding of humans that it manifests as injustice in human minds?

title: Item 87
statement: Non-believers need to show their own ideology is logical before Christians are obligated to assess the logical coherency of Christianity.

suggested_questions: Are the apparent improvements in the living conditions and economic stability of humans soon to give way to a more apocalyptic reality?
As long as a stable economy, declining per capita war deaths, and improvements in living conditions continue, can we conclude we are not close to the end times as described in the Bible?

title: Item 179
statement: Fallible humans have no grounds on which to judge whether God is loving based on His actions recorded in the Bible.
suggested_questions: Is comparing a particular God who is said to be loving against that same God's actions a moral question or a logical question?
If the God we've chosen gives assurances that his apparently unloving actions are actually loving, should we defer to His definition of "loving"?

title: Item 180
statement: The Bible has much to offer the progress of science.
suggested_questions: What are the domains of science in which a greater dependence on the Scriptures would result in greater discoveries?
Do the foundations of science require an understanding of the Bible?

It has often been suggested that we would not expect regularity in nature if the Bible had not suggested regularity in nature is the norm as opposed to continuous miraculous intervention. What scriptures might we index here, and why would the regularity in nature be invisible to the godless?

title: Item 181
statement: I enjoy engaging and countering secular arguments against Christianity.
suggested_questions: How might we strengthen our arguments against secular ideologies? Here are a few skills that might be considered: General critical thinking
Probability theory
Statistical acumen
An understanding of and practice in Bayes Theorem.
Rigorous standards of evidence
The philosophy of science
Knowledge of logical fallacies
Knowledge of cognitive biases
The history of science
General Philosophy
Knowledge of the original Biblical languages
Rhetorical skills

title: Item 182
statement: It is impossible for a soul to be annihilated. It must live in a conscious state for eternity.
suggested_questions: Is there something in the essence of a soul that makes the annihilation of that soul logically impossible?
Do some animals have eternal souls? Do any creatures have temporary souls?

title: Item 183
statement: It was impossible for Jesus to have sinned.
suggested_questions: If 1) Jesus was fully human and 2) humans have free will to sin, how is it logically possible that Jesus did not have this human free will to sin?

title: Item 184
statement: Mutual masturbation by a married couple is always sinful.
suggested_questions: Is it possible that self-masturbation is sinful, but mutual masturbation between married individuals is not? If so, elaborate.

title: Item 185
statement: Any consensual sex act within a heterosexual marriage is not intrinsically sinful.
suggested_questions: If you tend to respond negatively to this item, what consensual sex acts would be sinful? What standard was used in your conclusion?

title: Item 186
statement: Some kind of physical baptism is necessary for redemption.
suggested_questions: What forms of baptism are in obedience to the biblical mandate to be baptized?
Is there an actual biblical mandate to be physically baptized?

title: Item 187
statement: Since the Bible offers few cures for diseases that humans experience, we can conclude eliminating suffering is not a priority for God.
suggested_questions: If God intends for humans to scientifically reduce or eliminate physical suffering, why was Job intentionally made to suffer?

Had a short passage in the Bible been devoted to an explanation of the vaccinations, this would have eliminated an immense amount of human suffering. Is its absence not an indication that God does not give the alleviation of suffering much priority?

title: Item 188
statement: Researching and honestly considering arguments against Christianity is a healthy activity for most Christians.
suggested_questions: Should new Christians be encouraged to explore arguments against Christianity? Should they be accompanied by a seasoned Christian when venturing into this territory?
Is it possible for a real Christian to actually apostatize due to arguments against Christianity?

title: Item 189
statement: Redemption required that Jesus physically die.
suggested_questions: For what logical reason did the forgiveness of sin require a death?
Can we authentically forgive people who have wronged us only because Jesus died? What if the one forgiving feels no one should die or should have died for the forgiveness to be genuine?

title: Item 190
statement: Jesus physically rose from the dead in his earthly body.
suggested_questions: Is the type of body Jesus resurrected into an important doctrine? If so, why?
Did the resurrected body of Jesus need to carry the scars of His pre-death body? Will this be true for the resurrected bodies of Christian amputees?

title: Item 191
statement: Some humans with no belief in the Gospel will be redeemed.
suggested_questions: If you tend toward an affirmative response, can you give an explanation of what makes this possible?

title: Item 192
statement: I could be wrong in my belief that there is a personal God.
suggested_questions: Is anyone rational to claim they justifiably have no doubt that they are correct in their belief there is a personal God? (See Item #52 )
Is there an identifiable difference between the real Christian's confidence in their beliefs and the identical beliefs of a non-Christian who wrongly believes they are a Christian? (See Item #50 )

title: Item 193
statement: Becoming obese due to reasons other than a medical condition is sinful.
suggested_questions: Can we accurately identify Christians for whom their "God is their belly"? How should they be reprimanded?

title: Item 194
statement: I occasionally feel I do not actually believe in the Christian God.
suggested_questions: Are occasional seasons of doubt normal for real Christians. Or does doubt suggest one was never a real Christian?
If there is no chance a real Christian can apostatize, is doubt for a Christian a minor concern, bound to eventually dissipate?
Does the essence of rationality require that we hold at least a sliver of doubt about our beliefs?

title: Item 195
statement: It can sometimes be immoral not to divorce.
suggested_questions: Under what conditions would it be immoral not to divorce?
Is the abuse of one's own children such a case in which choosing not to divorce and merely separating would be immoral?

title: Item 196
statement: God chose to communicate the Gospel through the Bible since communicating to each human individually is not possible.
suggested_questions: What are the reasons God might have decided to avoid giving us indisputable evidence of his existence?

The Bible presented as an indirect divine revelation appears to be the same modus operandi of most popular false religions. Why might the omnipresent and omnipotent Christian God have chosen the same mode of communicating with humans?

title: Item 197
statement: Humans are held accountable for rejecting the Christian God even if they have not explicitly heard about the Christian God.
suggested_questions: If you answer this item affirmatively, how can culpability for the rejection of the Gospel fall on those who have not heard of the Gospel?
Can something coherently be rejected when it is unknown to the rejector?

title: Item 198
statement: Parents should give painful spankings to their children for misbehaving.
suggested_questions: For centuries, Christian parents spanked their children. Were they wrong, and did they have the ability to discern that they were wrong?
What form of corporal punishment, if any, is appropriate in Christian families today?

title: Item 199
statement: The average age at which the first damnable sin is committed ("age of accountability") is less than 10 years old.
suggested_questions: In your opinion, what age is the actual average age at which the first damnable sin is committed?
Is it wrong for parents to feel relieved that their child died before they became a conscious sinner?
Are there any identifiable clues when a child first becomes culpable and subject to damnation for their sins?

title: Item 200
statement: God sometimes speaks to me in a clear, audible voice.
suggested_questions: How might we categorize and interact with those who claim to hear the audible voice of God?
